title: MV Linux Mint 22.2 RMMV Crash with Project Load

posts.author: DJ990J
posts.body:
This issue started after I updated my Linux Mint from 22.2 to 22.3 Zena. At that time I realized the update was the issue and used time shift to go back to the previous version. Now it opens the RMMV, but won't stay open when I have any project loaded. I removed the compatibility layers and it never worked. It's currently on proton hotfix. I've tested the program on my laptop with the same Linux distro and I was able to get it to run and play test. The only difference is the graphic card. I've also updated the NW.js files as done here.​
How to update NW.js in RPG Maker MV (for RPG devs)
​
RPG Maker update Version 1.6.3
2 monitor setup

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
Thanks for taking the time to create a new thread and share some information about your system.
Since I am using Pop_OS, it's difficult for me to provide specific support regarding Mint.
That said, there are a couple of things that stand out to me.
Let's start with most likely to least likely.
RPG Maker, especially MV, regardless of operating system, doesn't like dual monitor set ups. If you had, at one point, moved the window to the secondary monitor and closed the software on that screen, it could cause it to crash. You'll need to make sure that the software is launching on your primary monitor.
To do this, the easiest way is to unplug the secondary monitor, restart the computer for good measure, then launch RPG Maker.
Secondly, NWJS does not need to be updated for RPG Maker to function on Linux. While it's still a good idea to update NWJS for performance reasons, make sure that the installation was done properly.
The guide you seemed to link looks fine (at least from my quick skimming), but double check you followed all the steps properly.
Thirdly, Nvidia drivers are notoriously unsupported on Linux, this is due to the fact that Nvidia does not open source the entirety of their driver suite - things such as PhysX, DLSS, and the like are closed source. Since Nvidia provides very weak driver support for their GPUs on Linux, this can cause some problems.
However, since you said it was working properly at one point and stopped working after an update, I'm not sure this is the likely culprit. Additionally, support for Nvidia GPUs on Linux has improved starting with your generation of cards (30 series) onward (though, still woefully lacking compared to Nvidia's Windows drivers)
My final guess is that perhaps some system information file - kind of like a registry key (not sure what the Linux equivalent is of that) may still be linked to Steam, RPG Maker, and the proton version - or other system settings.
I recommend doing a complete uninstall of RPG Maker. You don't need to delete your project files of course, but might as well back those up while you are in the process of messing with RPG Maker. Perform a clean installation of RPG Maker and ensure you do not enable Proton before you first launch of the software.
A clean installation will also remove the changes you made to NWJS, so you'll need to go through the update process again.

posts.author: DJ990J
posts.body: I reinstalled Linux, I now have 22.3 zara with a clean install. I downloaded steam, brave, then rpg maker mv. I opened RMMV without the proton layer and it didn't work. Tried again but switched on the layer to hot-fix proton. It came up but didn't respond. I then took the layer off again and the window pops up and everything is responsive BUT the play testing.

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
When you say that the play test is unresponsive, what exactly does it look like?
Does it crash and close out the play test window? Does it crash the whole software?
How are you launching the play test? Just the normal play test button? Via the "test event" context menu? Or battle test?
If the play test window stays open but is just black, can you open the console? Are there any errors printed there?
Some time ago - I think it's been over a year, if not 2, an update GGG pushed out to MV caused NWJS problems.
Since you reinstalled the whole OS, try updating your NWJS.
Linux is case sensitive with it's naming, so when you rename the test version of NWJS application, make sure it's 'Game' and not 'game'
This is what my NWJS folder looks like on Pop_OS (NWJS 69.1
(nice)
). The contents and naming should be the same.

posts.author: DJ990J
posts.body:
I click the play test button and nothing happens, same with the battle test. The main window is still up and functions fine. I updated the NWJS and I'm FINALLY back up!
Reinstalling Linux Mint then updating the NWJs files did the trick.
I hope this tread helps others! Thank you all for helping!
